feature: 9.8.1 Table 120 scope, identity, and family hints
source_location: Primary ISO/EC3 PDF Table 120, printed pp. 343–345 / physical pp. 358–360 (footer checked); §9.8.1 says descriptors apply to simple fonts and CIDFonts, not Type 0 fonts, and may be used with Type 3 beginning PDF 1.5. Markdown source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8340–8385.
errata: EC3 #11 clarifies FontName agreement for a Type 3 font that has /Name; otherwise it must agree with BaseFont. #337 (primary annotation physical p.360 / printed p.345) adds a contextual note: embedded descriptors describe the specific full/subset program, while a referenced font descriptor describes the source font material found by the writer at PDF creation. #178 adds a note that FontWeight is CSS-like but font formats may constrain it more. No sampled amendment changes FontFamily or FontStretch obligations.
ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml rows 9.8 and 9.8.1. The ledger notes Type 0 outer descriptors are not consumed and that FontFamily is consulted by rich-text family matching; it treats descriptor fields primarily as substitution information.
code_and_assertions: loading::opening resolves descriptors on simple-font and CIDFont-descendant paths; Type 0's outer descriptor is not used. FontName contributes to program/substitute identity and subset-prefix handling. FontFamily is not used as the font-family source in ordinary substitution (which derives from BaseFont); rich_text::layout uses it when matching a rich-text run against /DR. FontStretch contributes to substitute style. The wave53 harness reports PASS for substitute.rs::a_condensed_stretch_is_drawn_in_a_narrow_face and ::a_family_member_adds_only_style_words, and rich-text family matching has tests in crates/pdf-model/tests/rich_text.rs. The condensed-face test has an environment-dependent early return when no narrow face is installed; its harness PASS line alone does not prove that the assertion body ran.
verdict: sampled reader use is represented; the required dictionary shape and identity agreement are principally producer constraints, not a general requirement to reject malformed descriptors. FontFamily/FontStretch interpretation varies by font and substitution is a capability/policy choice.
residuals: No public test here checks each identity mismatch or demands a particular installed-family result. No mandatory reader error behavior is established by those producer constraints. The Type 3 name exception and rich-text consumer are bounded observations, not whole-field certification.

source_location: Primary ISO/EC3 PDF Table 120, printed pp. 343–345 / physical pp. 358–360; Table 121 and §9.8.2 continue at printed pp. 345–347 / physical pp. 360–362. Markdown source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8340–8440.
errata: #152 changes FontWeight to integer; #474 requires integer 1–1000, with hundreds only a SHOULD; #178 adds the CSS-like-weight qualification; #337 limits what embedded versus referenced descriptor metrics describe. Table 121's Symbolic bit is the recommended discriminator even for contradictory flag pairs. ForceBold determines whether extra pixels shall be considered, while thickening at small sizes is permitted.
ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.8.1 and §9.8.2 (around lines 2643–2651), plus the descriptor/substitution rows. The ledger maps weight and stem to substitute ranking, angle to slant, stretch/style bits to family/style selection, and states the writer-vs-reader distinction for flags.
code_and_assertions: substitute::Style::derive reads FontWeight, ItalicAngle, StemV and descriptor style bits for substitute requests; it does not promise a particular host face. Named unit assertions include substitute.rs::a_font_weight_is_read_as_the_nearest_class, ::a_stem_as_thick_as_a_bold_ones_is_drawn_in_a_bold_face, ::an_italic_angle_is_drawn_in_a_sloped_face, ::a_fixed_pitch_flag_is_drawn_in_a_fixed_pitch_face, and ::a_serif_flag_is_drawn_in_a_serifed_face. The weight assertion is deterministic; several family/face-selection tests contain environment-dependent early returns, so their wave53 PASS lines alone do not prove that assertions ran. metrics.rs::flag_tests check descriptor word bounds/bit extraction, while corpus `issue20232.pdf` checks public reporting for both Symbolic flags set.
verdict: selected fields reach real substitution behavior and have discriminating direct assertions. Ranking is product policy; writer type/range/bit constraints do not imply mandatory reader rejection. No missing raster ForceBold behavior is established because the source permits, rather than requires, small-size thickening.
residuals: No pixel assertion for ForceBold's small-device effect or exact face ranking is an ISO requirement. This review does not re-audit font appearance quality or every bit combination.

source_location: Primary ISO/EC3 PDF Table 120, printed pp. 343–345 / physical pp. 358–360. All dimensional values are in glyph space (§9.8.1); MissingWidth also feeds simple-font width behavior (§9.6.2). Markdown source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8340–8385.
errata: #190 changes Descent to ≤0 and adds a note that source font programs may express descent either sign while PDF expects nonpositive. #453 qualifies MissingWidth predictability: the specified result is predictable only when all uncovered character codes map to glyphs of the stated MissingWidth; otherwise behavior is implementation-dependent. #474/#152 apply to the FontWeight cell, not these metrics.
ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.8.1 (around line 2643), plus simple-font metric rows. Current finding 2038-D10 records that the ledger's MissingWidth explanation omits the #453 qualification; it is a ledger-erratum-qualification gap, not a runtime defect.
code_and_assertions: metrics::missing_width applies the stated value or Table 120's zero default; exact unit assertions are metrics.rs::a_stated_missing_width_is_the_width and ::an_absent_missing_width_is_zero. metrics::measured_extent / vertical_extent validate and consume Ascent/Descent; source-width and selection-band paths use width metrics. Current global findings contain D10 only for this family; expected-failures has no §9.8 descriptor failure. Exact named assertion PASS lines are present in scratchpad/r2038/spec-audit/eleven-crate-wave53.log: metrics::missing_width_tests::a_stated_missing_width_is_the_width and ::an_absent_missing_width_is_zero. The broader wave53 run had unrelated failures elsewhere, so it is not represented as a clean suite pass.
verdict: metric consumers and direct expected values are evidenced; the effective #453 clause permits deterministic choices for inconsistent widths and creates no reader rejection duty. D10 remains the sole current global font-descriptor finding.
residuals: The independent tests for MissingWidth establish parser/default policy, not the font-program precondition in #453. No test draft is supplied: asserting width consistency requires a separate known-font fixture and is not a demonstrated reader defect. The optional/producer fields FontBBox, Leading, CapHeight, XHeight, StemH, AvgWidth, and MaxWidth are not each required as runtime branches by this ledger claim.

source_location: Primary ISO/EC3 PDF Table 120, printed pp. 343–345 / physical pp. 358–360; embedded program formats continue in §9.9 and Table 124. Markdown source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8340–8385 and §9.9.
errata: Table 120 permits at most one of FontFile, FontFile2, and FontFile3. CharSet is meaningful only for Type 1 and deprecated in PDF 2.0. No sampled EC3 issue changes the one-program or CharSet scope wording.
ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.8.1 plus §9.9 embedded-program rows. Ledger represents parsing/refusal/substitution behavior and does not require rejecting every producer-invalid combination of program entries.
code_and_assertions: loading::opening/program routes to the applicable Type1, TrueType, or FontFile3 subtype parser. Current tests cover successful embedded-font drawing, unusable/empty program fallback, and archive-specific CharSet validation. Global test 2038-T11 records the added exact-xref same-host absent-program control; its named test `unreadable_program_falls_back_like_absent_program_and_keeps_its_report` passed in font-control-wave76.log. D51 is a stale fixed-document expectation, not descriptor behavior evidence.
verdict: the reader's supported program routes and substitution behavior have current assertions; producer's exclusivity and subset-list constraints are not automatically reader-error requirements. CharSet is metadata/validator-specific and not used for drawing selection.
residuals: The malformed multiple-program-entry case is not promoted as an expected failure. Full program-format conformance and all CharSet strings are outside this descriptor-cell pass.

source_location: Primary ISO/EC3 PDF Table 122 and §9.8.3, printed pp. 347–349 / physical pp. 362–364; Table 123 follows. Markdown source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8462–8505.
errata: EC3 #5 corrects §9.8.3.3's FD-key restriction: per-class descriptors can contain the Table 120 metric entries, excluding FontFile* and the Table 122 CIDFont-only entries. #337's note scopes metrics to the embedded program or the source material the writer selected for a referenced font; it does not add a reader validation requirement. PDF 2.0 adds Adobe-KR and marks Adobe-Japan2/Adobe-Korea1 deprecated in Table 123. CIDSet is optional and deprecated in PDF 2.0.
ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.8.3.1–.3 (around lines 2659–2683), including FD class override and Table 123 class behavior.
code_and_assertions: substitute::panose reads Style/Panose; substitute::language reads Lang; loading::class_faces applies per-class descriptors and substitute::glyph_classes consumes FD. Existing named assertions include panose.rs::the_clauses_own_example_classifies_a_light_serif_face, substitute.rs::a_lang_is_read_whether_the_producer_wrote_a_name_or_a_string, loading.rs::a_glyph_class_descriptor_chooses_the_face_for_its_own_class_alone, and glyph_class.rs::the_clauses_own_example_states_two_classes_and_both_are_applied. The class-face test contains environment-dependent early returns if the requested or distinguishing installed faces are unavailable; its wave53 PASS line alone does not establish the class override assertion executed. CIDSet is not consulted to select or draw glyphs.
verdict: the sampled substitute and class override choices are evidenced; fields are optional and mostly enable substitution policy, so omission/unsupported producer metadata does not imply a reader defect. EC3 #5 is a producer-key correction, not a new reject obligation.
residuals: No public PDF integration test specifically exercises Adobe-KR's new Table 123 row or parses CIDSet bits; no glyph-selection behavior is shown to depend on CIDSet. The audit is not a full class inventory certification.
